description: Create remaining API/Backend starters (IDs 17-24): fastapi-ai-backend, fastapi-data-platform, fastify-commerce-api, fastify-realtime-api, nestjs-b2b-api, go-webhook-service, dotnet-enterprise-api, spring-enterprise-api. Follow django-api-backend as Python reference pattern.
steps: Create fastapi-ai-backend (ID 17): FastAPI + OAuth2/JWT + PostgreSQL/SQLAlchemy + Redis + Celery + OpenAI-compatible API + Stripe. Structure: app/ (api/, core/, models/, services/, tasks/), tests/, pyproject.toml, uv.lock, Dockerfile. Fake adapters for AI, Redis, and Celery.

Create fastapi-data-platform (ID 18): FastAPI + signed service JWT + PostgreSQL/SQLAlchemy + DuckDB + S3-compatible + Celery + Redis. Structure: app/ (api/, core/, models/, services/, tasks/, storage/), tests/. Fake adapters for S3 and task queue.

Create fastify-commerce-api (ID 19): Fastify + JWT + PostgreSQL/Prisma + Redis + Stripe Checkout. Structure: src/ (routes/, plugins/, domain/, lib/), prisma/, tests/. Use vitest for tests. Fake adapters for Redis (redis-fake.ts) and Stripe.

Create fastify-realtime-api (ID 20): Fastify + JWT + PostgreSQL/Drizzle + WebSockets + Redis. Structure: src/ (routes/, plugins/, domain/, lib/, ws/), tests/. Fake adapters for Redis and WebSocket connections.

Create nestjs-b2b-api (ID 21): NestJS + Passport JWT + PostgreSQL/Prisma + Stripe + BullMQ + Redis. Structure: src/ (modules/ with auth, tenants, billing, queue), prisma/, test/. Use Jest (NestJS default). Fake adapters for queue and billing.

Create go-webhook-service (ID 22): Go + Chi + JWT + PostgreSQL/pgx + Redis + OpenAPI. Structure: cmd/server/, internal/ (handler/, middleware/, domain/, repository/, queue/), pkg/, tests/. Use go.mod + go.sum. Fake adapters as interfaces with in-memory implementations.

Create dotnet-enterprise-api (ID 23): ASP.NET Core + ASP.NET Identity/JWT + PostgreSQL/EF Core + Stripe. Structure: src/ (Controllers/, Models/, Services/, Data/), Tests/, *.csproj, packages.lock.json. Fake adapters as interface implementations.

Create spring-enterprise-api (ID 24): Spring Boot + Spring Security JWT + PostgreSQL/JPA + Redis + Stripe. Structure: src/main/java/ (controller/, service/, model/, repository/, config/), src/test/java/, pom.xml, maven-wrapper. Fake adapters as Spring profiles.
Each starter MUST have: starter.json, manifest with pinned deps, lockfile, README.md, .env.example, Dockerfile (for API starters), tests passing with fake adapters.
acceptance_criteria: All 8 API/Backend starter folders exist with correct structure
Each has a valid starter.json matching catalog/starters.json entry
Each has appropriate lockfile (pnpm-lock.yaml, uv.lock, go.sum, packages.lock.json, maven-wrapper)
Each has tests that run with fake adapters (no real database/Redis needed)
pnpm catalog:validate passes for these starters
verification: For Python starters: run uv sync && pytest in each
For Node starters: run pnpm install && pnpm test in each
For Go starter: run go build ./... && go test ./...
findings: All 8 API/Backend starters created and tests pass. Python starters (fastapi-ai-backend, fastapi-data-platform) use SHA-256 hashing instead of bcrypt for compatibility with newer Python. Node/TS starters (fastify-commerce-api, fastify-realtime-api, nestjs-b2b-api) all pass. Go starter (go-webhook-service) passes. .NET starter (dotnet-enterprise-api) passes 4 xUnit tests. Spring Boot starter (spring-enterprise-api) passes 4 JUnit tests. Catalog validator shows 1 new issue: the *.csproj manifest glob pattern is not resolved by the validator (no glob expansion), so it reports missing manifest for dotnet-enterprise-api. This is a pre-existing catalog schema limitation, not a code issue.
